title: Switching a headache clinic from paper to app diaries: costs and consequences for the clinic and the preventive budget
subtitle: Which question first: diary effectiveness or the costs of the switch
statement: About a third of the clinic's 1,900 migraine patients a year arrive without a usable paper diary, which lengthens appointments and delays decisions about injectable preventives. The clinic will switch to a free app diary in January 2027. The investigator must choose between testing whether the app improves diaries and decisions, and working out what the switch costs and saves, including its effect on the preventive drug budget.
whoAffected: Adults with migraine attending the clinic, especially older patients and those without smartphones; clinic nurses and neurologists; the health board's drug budget holders.
whatHurts: Appointments spent reconstructing headache days, weeks of delay before effective prevention, and patients who cannot use an app being left behind.
currentPractice: Paper diaries for eight weeks before each appointment; no check of usability before the visit.
whyNow: The switch date is fixed for January 2027, so data from before and after will exist.
constraints: Four hours a week of one clinic nurse from November 2026 to October 2027; existing clinic activity, booking and pharmacy data only; no change to the clinic manager's switch date of January 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient arrives with a usable diary in a format they can manage, and eligible patients start prevention without avoidable delay.
summary: Problem framed around two candidate questions; the inferred economic family stands until the investigator chooses.
